match_note: arXiv v1 (24 Aug 2026) appears to be the revised manuscript, not the one first reviewed. The peer review file title is 'Parity-dependent coupling of topological edge states to a superconductor in molecular Haldane chains' while v1 is titled 'Parity-dependent coupling of molecular spin chains to a superconductor'. v1 already contains the changes the rebuttal promises: 'S=1 many-body spin excitations' wording (R3's request), the incipient YSR signal at N=12 (Fig. S12) that the rebuttal says was 'pointed out in the revised version', J_K variations attributed to the Au(111) herringbone reconstruction with new references, the N=8 dehydrogenation removing the ST peak (Fig. S16), the BLBQ model in Section S6, and a closing remark on regimes where edge entanglement and superconducting screening coexist. The underlying data and claims (chains N=2-14 on Au/Nb(110), odd/even YSR alternation, two-site model, Fig. 3d spread) are the same, so in_v1 is judged on whether the topic of each concern is present. Rounds: Version 0 had R1, R2, R3; Version 1 had R1 only, satisfied.

concerns.quote: the experimental series appears to terminate at the onset of this crossover regime, with N = 14 being the longest even chain reported and exhibiting only an incipient YSR signal.
concerns.summary: The claimed long-chain decoupled-edge regime is not reached; longer even chains are needed to show YSR screening emerging in even-parity chains.

concerns.quote: Such a comparison would help clarify whether the observed behavior reflects a genuine manipulation of an existing edge-state pair or effects associated with a change in parity and boundary conditions.
concerns.summary: Passivating one edge changes the chain's parity and boundary condition, so passivated even chains should be compared with intrinsic odd chains to rule out that explanation.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: it would be useful if the authors could discuss the physical origin of the observed JK variations. Clarifying the relative importance of JK fluctuations compared with the systematic evolution of J(N)
concerns.summary: The spread of YSR binding energies at fixed length is attributed to J_K variations without a physical origin or comparison with the systematic J(N) trend.

concerns.quote: The authors should specify how many N = 14 chains were investigated, how many exhibited detectable YSR resonances, and whether the displayed spectrum is representative of the full population.
concerns.summary: The YSR emergence in even N=14 chains rests on unclear statistics; chain counts and binding-energy spread are needed.

concerns.quote: many tunneling spectra are presented without the corresponding acquisition positions being explicitly indicated in the figure panels.
concerns.summary: Spectra acquisition positions should be marked systematically, since spatial localization is central to the interpretation.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: it is not entirely clear how reproducible the extracted excitation energies are across different chains of identical length.
concerns.summary: The uncertainty and chain-to-chain reproducibility of the collective spin mode energies are not reported.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: the caption notes that a small number of measurements fall outside the mapped theoretical range. A brief discussion of the possible origin of these deviations would be helpful.
concerns.summary: Some YSR binding energies in Fig. 3d lie outside the model's predicted range and this is not explained.

concerns.quote: The previous work by Mishra et al. , where triangulene chains on Au (no superconductor), concluded that fractionalization occurs for odd chain numbers. ... Therefore, the fractionalization is not completely novel.
concerns.summary: Edge fractionalization in triangulene chains was already shown by Mishra et al., so only the superconducting-substrate aspect is new, and suitability for Nature is left to the editor.

concerns.quote: the results of dehydrogenation of the triangulene could be presented more prominent in the main part. It is a nice achievement and is now in the supplementary part.
concerns.summary: The dehydrogenation (edge passivation) results deserve a place in the main text rather than the supplement.

concerns.quote: the excitations that the authors are measuring are not just magnons, but rather confined excitations of the incoherent many-body excitation continuum.
concerns.summary: Calling the inelastic excitations 'magnonic' is imprecise for an S=1 chain with an excitation continuum; 'S=1 many-body spin excitations' is suggested.

concerns.quote: whether their experiments allow discerning features of a regime in which entanglement between edge spins and screening with the superconductor coexist.
concerns.summary: The authors should comment on whether the data reveal a regime where inter-edge entanglement and superconducting screening coexist.
